m.n: The Sacrament of the Eucharist (First Holy Communion)

co.n: The Sacrament of the Eucharist (First Holy Communion) Cohort

c.p: What is the outward sign and theological effect of Holy Communion?
c.a: body and blood of christ | body and blood | eucharist | real presence
c.h: Think about the Last Supper and the words of consecration spoken by the priest.
c.e: The Eucharist is the source and summit of Christian life, representing the Real Presence of Christ in His Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity (CCC 1324).
r: Catholic doctrine teaches transubstantiation—the bread and wine substantially become the Real Presence of Christ, not mere symbols.

c.p: What is transubstantiation in Catholic Eucharistic theology?
c.a: the change of the whole substance of bread and wine into the body and blood of christ | change of substance into christ's body and blood | substantial change into the body and blood of christ
c.h: The physical appearances (accidents) of bread and wine remain, but their underlying reality is transformed.
c.e: Through the words of consecration and the Holy Spirit, transubstantiation occurs: the reality of the bread and wine becomes the living Christ (Council of Trent; CCC 1376).
r: Catholic teaching affirms that the Eucharist is not merely a symbolic memorial, but the objective Real Presence of Jesus Christ.

c.p: How must a Catholic prepare to receive Holy Communion worthily?
c.a: be in a state of grace and observe the eucharistic fast for one hour | state of grace and fast for one hour | free from mortal sin and fast
c.h: Think about spiritual readiness (free from grave sin) and physical fasting before receiving.
c.e: Catholics must fast from food and drink (except water and medicine) for at least one hour before Communion and be in a state of grace, seeking confession if conscious of mortal sin (CCC 1385–1387).
r: fasting for three whole days without water
The Church asks for a fast of one hour from food and liquids prior to receiving, not three days, and water is always permitted.
